boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a first-person emphatic pivot, “For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages” (web:Isa.66.18), moving the subject from judgment on apostates to a universal ingathering: survivors sent to far-off nations (66:19), all Israel's brothers brought as an offering (66:20), priests and Levites selected even from among them (66:21). It closes on a permanence assurance echoing the new-creation declaration of 65:17, "הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.22, 'the new heavens and the new earth'), sealed by the closing signature "נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) ('says Yahweh'). The unit ends there because 66:23 opens a new temporal formula ('from one new moon to another') describing recurring worship rather than the one-time ingathering event.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a recurring-time formula distinct from the one-time ingathering event of the preceding unit, “It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” (web:Isa.66.23), rendered in Hebrew as "יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) ('all flesh will come to worship'). The book's very last verse turns from that universal worship to a grim closing image, “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched” (web:Isa.66.24), rendered "תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) ('their worm will not die'). This couplet is kept as its own unit because it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24) and because its own internal turn -- from universal worship to unending punishment of the transgressors -- is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it.
